title: Talking to Web Services
text: These questions check that you can read an API request, work with a JSON reply, handle errors without hiding them, and keep secrets out of your code.

choices: A name in the query string, with the value precipitation_sum

tasks.text: A trigger runs a function whose only error handling is catch (error) { Logger.log(error) }. The weather service is down. What appears on the Executions page?
choices: Completed, as if nothing went wrong

tasks.text: Where should a Discord webhook address be kept?
choices: In a constant at the top of Code.gs
In the prompt you send your assistant

tasks.text: Give two ways a script that fetches a forecast every morning could fail, even if its code is correct.
tasks.answer: Any two: the service is down or unreachable; the internet connection fails; the service returns an error; the service changes its reply format or parameter names; a rate limit or changed terms.

tasks.text: You want to ask an assistant why your webhook code fails. What should you do with the webhook address before pasting the code, and why?
tasks.answer: Replace it with a placeholder (e.g. YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL), because anyone with the address can post to the channel, and anything pasted into a chat may be stored. If it leaks, delete it and create a new one.

tasks.text: Write a function needsWatering(rainMm, thresholdMm) that returns true if the rain is less than the threshold, and false otherwise. Then write testNeedsWatering, which logs the result for 0 and 2, 1.7 and 2, and 2 and 2. (Expected: true, true, false.)

Start a new chat with your updated learner profile. Ask for a script that uses Open-Meteo to log tomorrow's maximum temperature for the garden's location (use a latitude and longitude of your choice), with error handling that doesn't hide failures. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Check the address's parameter names against Open-Meteo's documentation (open-meteo.com). Are they right? (3) What happens in the catch block? Would a failure show on the Executions page? (4) Run it in Apps Script and report the result.
tasks.answer: Full credit: parameter names checked against the documentation (e.g. daily=temperature_2m_max); the catch block is evaluated for whether it rethrows or notifies; result reported. Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
